title: Investigating Whether Inspect AI Evaluations Reproduce Across Compute Environments
original_idea: Run the same Inspect AI evaluation suite on the same model in three configurations (local GPU, different batch sizes, quantized vs. full precision). Measure variance in scores.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Reproducibility is important but is more of a methodological hygiene issue than a fundamental safety insight. Impact is moderate.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Running Inspect AI is documented but requires setting up multiple compute configurations, understanding quantization, and managing GPU environments. Moderate complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three configurations, one model, one evaluation suite. Clear and bounded. Feasible in 30 hours if Inspect AI setup is smooth.

novelty.reasoning: Red Hat ran over half a million evaluations on quantized LLMs (2024) demonstrating that quantization degrades performance variably across tasks. Framework-level consistency issues between vLLM and HuggingFace Transformers are documented in GitHub issues (vllm-project/vllm#1069). However, no published study specifically examines Inspect AI evaluation suite reproducibility across compute configurations (local GPU, different batch sizes, quantized vs. full precision). The Inspect AI framework is relatively new (UK AISI), and its specific reproducibility properties under varying compute environments have not been characterized. This is a practical and timely contribution to evaluation infrastructure reliability.

evidence: Red Hat. We Ran Over Half a Million Evaluations on Quantized LLMs. Red Hat Developer, 2024.
